sections.title: Medi-Cal (California Medicaid)
sections.blurb: Free comprehensive coverage for Californians with MAGI up to 138% FPL. The most important fact for you: eligibility is based on total countable income (tax rules), there is NO asset/savings test, and no work requirement is in effect until January 1, 2027.

rows.finding: Adults ages 19–64, California residents, with MAGI up to 138% of the federal poverty level. Applies whether or not you have children, and with or without any job.
rows.source_label: DHCS — Medi-Cal: Eligibility by Federal Poverty Level / Qualify
rows.note: DHCS is the state Medicaid agency.

rows.finding: DHCS publishes $22,025/year ($1,836/month) at 138% FPL for a household of one for 2026 (based on the 2026 HHS poverty guideline of $15,960; 138% = $22,024.80, rounded).
rows.source_label: DHCS Eligibility-by-FPL chart; HHS ASPE 2026 Poverty Guidelines
rows.note: 2026 FPL source: https://aspe.hhs.gov/topics/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines (also Federal Register 91 FR, Jan 15, 2026).

rows.source_label: DHCS Eligibility by FPL chart

rows.topic: No asset or savings test (MAGI categories)
rows.finding: For MAGI Medi-Cal (adults 19–64, children, parents, pregnant), DHCS's own comparison table says "No property limits" — bank balances, savings, cars and investment accounts are NOT counted. Only non-MAGI categories (65+, blind/disabled, long-term care) test property, and even there California raised limits to $130,000 (single)/$195,000 (couple) effective Jan 1, 2026.
rows.source_label: DHCS — Medi-Cal Help Center (MAGI vs Non-MAGI table); DHCS Medi-Cal Changes

rows.finding: No work/community-engagement requirement applies to Medi-Cal adults in 2026. The new federal requirement (H.R.1 §71119, P.L. 119-21) first applies January 1, 2027 — see the New Laws page for exactly how you could satisfy it with non-wage income.
rows.source_label: CMS — Community Engagement IFR fact sheet (Jun 1, 2026)

rows.finding: Medi-Cal is free or low-cost coverage. Most members keep the full benefit set: doctor, hospital, emergency, prescriptions, mental health/addiction care, checkups/vaccines, long-term care, rides to appointments, dentist, eye exams/glasses.
rows.value: $0 typical premium for adults expansion group
rows.source_label: DHCS — Medi-Cal Changes (benefits summary)
rows.note: Covered CA also describes Medi-Cal as 'free or low-cost': https://www.coveredca.com/health/medi-cal/

rows.finding: Medi-Cal applications can be submitted year-round. Eligibility and the coverage start date are determined by the county under applicable monthly-income, household and program rules; a trading loss or temporary vacancy by itself is not an immediate entitlement.
rows.source_label: DHCS — Apply for Medi-Cal
rows.note: See 42 CFR 435.603(h)(1) for current-month MAGI methodology; do not infer a county determination or immediate start.

rows.finding: A single Covered California application determines whether you get subsidized private coverage or Medi-Cal; households can be split across programs ("mixed-program family"). Apply at apply.coveredca.com or your county social services office.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Open Enrollment ("One application covers both")

rows.finding: Children (0–18) eligible up to 266% FPL; pregnant individuals up to 213% FPL; Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP) covers higher incomes for pregnant individuals; 2026 single-person amounts: 213% = $33,995, 266% = $42,454 (Covered CA 2027 chart, DHCS ACWDL 26-01 figures).
rows.source_label: Covered California — Program Eligibility by FPL chart (PDF)

rows.finding: DHCS eligibility letters (e.g., MEDIL 24-02) reference an ACA group covering adults 19–64 at 138% FPL and separate treatment for older adults; California also runs Medi-Cal access for low-income seniors 65+ without share-of-cost. If you are age 60+, confirm your exact group with the county/DHCS.
rows.source_label: DHCS MEDIL 24-02 (eligibility groups PDF)
rows.note: Flag FL-09. Do not rely on this row for an age-based plan until confirmed.

rows.topic: 2026 immigration-status changes (not applicable to U.S. citizens)
rows.finding: Effective Jan 1, 2026 California froze new full-scope Medi-Cal sign-ups for certain non-citizen groups, with fee-for-service transition, restricted dental and monthly premiums for those groups in 2027. A U.S. citizen is not subject to any of these; listed so you can rule it out.
rows.source_label: DHCS — Medi-Cal Changes

sections.title: Covered California (the state Marketplace)
sections.blurb: Subsidized private plans when income is above the Medi-Cal line. This is where the 2026 federal subsidy changes hit hardest — and where California has substituted state money for lower-income enrollees.

rows.finding: To buy a plan: be a California resident, be a U.S. citizen/national (lawfully present residents also qualify), not be incarcerated, and meet income thresholds for help. There is NO employment or work requirement for Marketplace financial help.
rows.value: Citizenship + residency + income; no job test
rows.source_label: Covered California — Eligibility Guidelines
rows.note: Eligibility factors published: household, income, residency, citizenship/immigration, current coverage, age/disability factors.

rows.finding: Federal premium tax credits generally require household income between 100% and 400% of the plan-year applicable FPL, plus other eligibility requirements. For a single person in 2026 Covered California uses $62,600 at 400% FPL; the $63,840 400% figure applies to 2027 marketplace plans.
rows.source_label: Covered California — 2026 Enrollment Dashboard; IRS PTC eligibility

rows.finding: The ARPA/IRA enhanced premium tax credits (which set contribution as low as 0% to 150% FPL and removed the 400% cliff) expired Dec 31, 2025 and were not renewed by Congress. Covered CA: "Monthly costs may be higher now, but some plans still cost as little as $10 per month."
rows.source_label: Covered California — Important Changes
rows.note: Also stated in Covered CA's 2026 open-enrollment press release (Feb 26, 2026).

rows.source_label: Covered California HBEX — Financial Help Basics Quick Guide (official stakeholder doc)

rows.topic: California Premium Subsidy 2026 (state money replacing lost federal help)
rows.finding: For 2026 California appropriated $190M (Health Care Affordability Reserve Fund) to hold the line for low-income enrollees: households ≤165% FPL who get APTC also get the state subsidy; required share is held at 0% of income up to 150% FPL and 3.19%–3.91% for 150–165% (vs the federal 4.19–4.91%). State subsidy is reconciled with the California FTB at tax time.
rows.source_label: Covered CA State Premium Subsidy Policy Explainer (Feb 2026) + HBEX Financial Help Basics
rows.note: Program requires applying through the subsidized Covered CA application and being APTC-eligible.

rows.finding: For 2027 the Legislature raised HCARF funding to $300M and expanded the state subsidy to households up to 200% FPL (2026-guideline figures: $31,920 individual / $66,000 family of 4). 2027 required-share schedule: 0% up to 138% and 138–150% FPL; 2.8%–5.28% (>150–200%); 6.78%–8.66% (>200–250%); 8.66%–10.22% (>250–300%); 10.22% (300–400%); no help above 400%. ~200,000 people can choose Silver plans with a $0 premium.
rows.source_label: Covered CA 2027 FPL chart + Rates & Plans press release (Jul 21, 2026) + 2027 subsidy insight
rows.note: Percentages from https://www.coveredca.com/pdfs/FPL-chart.pdf ("Percent of income paid for premiums" table). 2027 rates (avg +9.9%) are preliminary pending DHCO review — see flag FL-07.

rows.finding: Cost-sharing reductions are available to eligible marketplace enrollees who choose an Enhanced Silver plan and meet income and other criteria (generally up to 250% FPL). They are not automatically available throughout the full 100–400% federal premium-tax-credit income band.
rows.value: Eligible Enhanced Silver applicants, generally ≤250% FPL
rows.source_label: Covered California — Financial Help (Enhanced Silver)

rows.finding: Open enrollment runs Nov 1 – Jan 31 each year. For 2027 coverage: applications open Nov 1, 2026; enroll by Dec 31, 2026 for a Jan 1, 2027 start; enroll in January 2027 for Feb 1 start. The 2026 period (Nov 1, 2025–Jan 31, 2026) closed with 1.9M+ sign-ups/renewals.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Open Enrollment; Feb 26, 2026 press release

rows.finding: Outside open enrollment you can enroll after major life changes (losing coverage, marriage, move to California, etc.) — normally 60 days from the event. Moving to California from another state is a qualifying move.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Open Enrollment (SEP section); HealthCare.gov SEP glossary

rows.topic: You report ESTIMATED income — volatile trading years matter
rows.finding: Financial help is based on the household income you project for the coverage year. If you under-estimate, you may have to repay excess credit at tax time (Form 8962 with 1040; 1095-A from the insurer); over-estimating costs you subsidy you were owed. Covered CA's guidance: keep income updated during the year.
rows.source_label: Covered California — What is financial help? (steps 1–4)

rows.topic: NEW: APTC repayment is no longer capped
rows.finding: From the 2026 tax year (returns filed in 2027), excess advance premium tax credit must be repaid IN FULL — the old income-based repayment caps were repealed (P.L. 119-21). For traders this raises the stakes of under-estimating a winning year: if actual MAGI ends up far above the estimate, the clawback is unlimited.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Important Changes; IRS — Working Families Tax Cuts overview
rows.note: IRS overview: "Removal of limitations on repayment of excess advance payment of the premium tax credit for tax years beginning after Dec. 31, 2025."

rows.topic: Strategy: take the credit at tax time instead of monthly
rows.finding: Applicants may reduce or decline advance monthly assistance and claim the full Premium Tax Credit when filing (Form 8962 + 1095-A); you can also change the APTC amount applied monthly at any time during the year. Useful when you can't predict trading results: you buy at full monthly premium and true-up via the credit, avoiding a large repayment.
rows.value: APTC % is adjustable / can take lump sum
rows.source_label: Covered California HBEX — Financial Help Basics Quick Guide
rows.note: IRS Pub 974 (Premium Tax Credit) also referenced there: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p974

rows.topic: NEW: income documentation rules arrive for 2028
rows.finding: Beginning with the 2028 plan year (effective Jan 1, 2028 per Covered CA), consumers must prove eligibility for financial help before it is applied, and those who don't confirm/update information will not be auto re-enrolled with financial help.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Important Changes

rows.finding: Applicants under 30 (no age limit for hardship exemption) may buy a Minimum Coverage (catastrophic) plan; for 2026 in California it qualifies as an HDHP (HSA-eligible) and receives the $1/month state premium credit but not APTC/CSR.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Eligibility Guidelines & HBEX Financial Help Basics

rows.topic: 400% FPL references differ for 2026 and 2027 marketplace plans
rows.finding: For a one-person household Covered California lists 2026 marketplace 400% FPL as $62,600 and 2027 marketplace 400% FPL as $63,840. Above the applicable plan-year line, federal APTC is generally unavailable; individual cost must be obtained from a plan quote. Other eligibility conditions still apply.
rows.source_label: Covered California — 2026 Enrollment Dashboard, Financial Details

rows.topic: Immigrant eligibility changes (not applicable to you)
rows.finding: From Jan 1, 2027 Covered CA financial help will be limited to an "Eligible Non-Citizen" definition (LPR/green card, Cuban/Haitian entrant, Freely Associated States citizens, etc.). U.S. citizens' eligibility is unaffected.
rows.source_label: Covered CA HBEX — Financial Help Basics; Covered CA Important Changes
rows.note: Listed so you can confirm the change does not apply to your status.

sections.title: Action Plan (sequenced, each step sourced)
sections.blurb: The concrete path from where you are today (Oct 18, 2026 — after the 2026 window closed, before the 2027 window opens Nov 1) to coverage, plus how to handle the work requirement when it arrives.

rows.finding: Gather an honest projection of 2027 household taxable income and MAGI. Taxable rental result depends on expenses/loss rules; interest depends on statements; this taxpayer's Kalshi tax classification and gain/loss accounting are unresolved. The $22,025 Medi-Cal single-person reference is for 2026, not a published 2027 Medi-Cal FPL limit. Ask the county/exchange for a determination using current rules.
rows.source_label: DHCS — 2026 Medi-Cal monthly FPL chart (does not set 2027)
rows.note: Tax treatment: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p527 and https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550 . Do not treat this row as a numeric 2027 eligibility determination.

rows.topic: Step 2A — If estimated MAGI ≤ 138% FPL: Medi-Cal, apply anytime
rows.finding: If actual county MAGI and program factors make you eligible, Medi-Cal applications are accepted year-round and no earned wages are required. The county determines eligibility and effective coverage; no immediate enrollment or specific group is guaranteed.
rows.source_label: DHCS — Apply for Medi-Cal

rows.topic: Step 2B — If 138%–200% FPL: Covered CA with 0%–~5% contributions
rows.finding: If eligible for a 2027 Covered California plan, federal APTC and the state premium subsidy may reduce the premium, with state assistance announced to 200% FPL ($31,920 for one person) for eligible applicants. Enhanced Silver cost-sharing reductions require Silver selection and other criteria. Compare your actual annual household income and available plans; no premium is promised.
rows.source_label: Covered California — 2027 rate and state subsidy announcement

rows.topic: Step 2C — If >200% FPL: compare subsidized (to 400%) vs full price
rows.finding: Above 200% FPL, compare plan and APTC eligibility under the 2027 plan-year chart; beyond 400% FPL, request a full-price quote. An HSA deduction is available only if personally eligible under IRS rules and cannot be assumed merely from no wages or a Bronze label; seek tax guidance before relying on any income-reduction approach.
rows.value: Plan quote / tax eligibility not provided
rows.source_label: Covered California — 2027 FPL chart

rows.topic: Step 3 — Enroll by the right date
rows.finding: Enroll by Dec 31, 2026 for a Jan 1, 2027 effective date; enroll Jan 1–31, 2027 for Feb 1 start. Miss the window entirely and you wait for a Special Enrollment Period (60 days after a qualifying event) or the next OEP.
rows.source_label: Covered California — Open Enrollment

rows.topic: Step 4 — Set the APTC dial for volatility
rows.finding: If you can't predict your trading year, either (a) apply with a conservative-but-honest estimate and promptly report expected changes, or (b) take less/no advance credit monthly and claim the credit at filing — now that repayment is uncapped from the 2026 tax year, err toward accuracy.
rows.source_label: Covered CA HBEX Financial Help Basics; Covered CA Important Changes

rows.topic: Step 5 — Reconcile both credits at tax time
rows.finding: Use the insurer's Form 1095-A to file IRS Form 8962 (federal APTC) and reconcile the California Premium Subsidy with the Franchise Tax Board on your CA return, per Covered CA's program design. Keep Kalshi P&L statements + 1099s as the income record.
rows.source_label: Covered CA HBEX Financial Help Basics Quick Guide

rows.topic: Step 6 — Prepare for the 2027 Medi-Cal work rule (if enrolled)
rows.finding: Starting Jan 1, 2027, adults subject to the Medi-Cal community-engagement rule may show at least $580 monthly household income calculated with MAGI-based methods, qualifying activities/education or a statutory exception. At application the preceding month matters; at redetermination a month since the last determination. The six-month average is for seasonal workers, not any fluctuating trading or rent. DHCS dates six-month financial eligibility checks to March 1, 2027.
rows.value: $580 MAGI-based monthly income / other qualifying route; individual result unknown
rows.source_label: California AB 2161 — WIC §14005.69(d)–(g)

rows.topic: Step 7 — Use free help and official screening tools
rows.finding: Covered CA: Shop & Compare estimates costs before applying; certified enrollers assist free of charge ((800) 300-1506). DHCS publishes an eligibility estimator and county office directory. No fee — avoid paid "navigator" services.
rows.source_label: Covered CA — Get help; DHCS — Qualify / Find a county office

rows.topic: Step 8 — Keep California's individual mandate satisfied
rows.finding: Whichever route you take, full-year Medi-Cal or a Marketplace plan is minimum essential coverage → no state penalty (check line 92 box on Form 540). If uninsured for part of a year, the "unaffordable coverage" and "below filing threshold" exemptions may still zero it — claim exemptions on FTB Form 3853 or via a Covered CA exemption certificate.
rows.source_label: FTB — Personal Health Care Mandate
